cases.name: 1040-pairs_in_either_order

cases.name: 1050-block_comment_holding_line_comment

cases.name: 1080-block_close_touching_a_line_comment

cases.name: 1090-block_comment_closed_after_a_line_comment

cases.name: 1100-close_touching_reopen_plain

cases.name: 1140-three_slashes_are_one_comment

cases.name: 2050-string_opening_after_block_close

cases.name: 2060-backtick_template_holding_a_comment
cases.trap: a line comment symbol inside a template literal is text

cases.name: 2070-verbatim_string_crossing_lines

cases.name: 2080-odd_triple_quote_count

cases.trap:
the # inside the docstring is text and not a comment symbol, and the docstring around it is a

cases.name: 2100-triple_quoted_data_not_documentation

cases.name: 2110-here_string_holding_an_apostrophe

cases.name: 2130-raw_string_holding_quotes
cases.trap:
a Rust raw string, opened with r#" and closed with "#, so the plain quotes written inside it are

cases.name: 2140-raw_string_holding_its_own_closing_bracket
cases.trap:
a C++ raw string, R"( to )", holding a block comment opener on a line of its own. Only the raw

cases.name: 2150-delimited_raw_string_names_its_own_closer

a C++ raw string that puts a word of its own between the R" and the bracket, and then ends only at

cases.name: 2170-lua_level_bracket_holding_plain_close
cases.trap:
Lua opens a long comment with any number of equals signs between its brackets, and only a closer

cases.name: 2180-lua_short_closer_hiding_the_real_one
cases.trap:
a Lua comment opened with one equals sign, ended by a line reading ]]=]. The bare ]] at the front

cases.name: 2190-triple_quote_read_as_three_short_ones

Groovy opens a string that runs over several lines with three apostrophes. A counter that reads

cases.name: 3010-escaped_quote_before_comment
cases.trap:
an escaped quote does not close the string, so the // after it is a real comment and not text

cases.name: 3020-multiline_string_ending_in_backslash
cases.trap:
a raw string whose last byte is a backslash, written with the same symbol at both ends. A

cases.name: 3030-raw_string_ending_in_backslash
cases.trap:
a Rust raw string, r#" to "#, whose last character is a backslash. Nothing escapes inside a raw

cases.name: 3050-verbatim_string_ending_in_a_backslash
cases.trap:
a verbatim string whose last byte is a backslash. In F# the body of @"..." is literal, so the

cases.name: 3070-backslash_before_a_closing_quote_in_sql
cases.trap: standard SQL escapes a quote by doubling it and the backslash is an ordinary character

cases.name: 3080-backtick_escapes_inside_a_double_quoted_string
cases.trap:
the backtick is what escapes inside PowerShell's double quoted string, so the quote in the middle

cases.name: 3090-backtick_before_a_single_quoted_string
cases.trap:
the other PowerShell string form escapes nothing inside itself, so the backtick can only speak

cases.name: 4010-char_literal_holding_a_quote
cases.trap:
a Rust character literal holding a double quote. The quote is the value of the character and opens
no string, so the comment lines under it are comments

cases.name: 4020-two_char_literals_holding_escapes
cases.trap:
two character literals on one line, one holding an escaped backslash and one holding a quote.
Ordinary Rust that any escaping routine is written with, and not a line contrived for this suite

cases.name: 4030-character_written_with_a_backslash
cases.trap:
Clojure writes a character as a backslash and the character itself, so a double quote is written

cases.name: 4040-escaped_apostrophe_outside_quotes
cases.trap:
a backslash before an apostrophe in unquoted shell text, which is how one writes an apostrophe

cases.name: 4050-lifetime_and_apostrophe_in_string
cases.trap:
two lone apostrophes on one Rust line: the one that marks a lifetime, and the one in the word

cases.name: 4060-primed_identifier_haskell
cases.trap:
Haskell lets a name end in an apostrophe, so x' is one name and the apostrophe opens nothing. The

cases.name: 4070-primed_identifier_ocaml
cases.trap:
OCaml lets a name end in an apostrophe, so x' is one name and the apostrophe opens nothing. The
line under it holds a real character literal, and the comment under that is written with (* *),

cases.name: 4080-primed_identifier_and_apostrophe
cases.trap:
F# lets a name end in an apostrophe, so s' is one name. The apostrophe in the word it's, inside the
string on the same line, is the other one. Neither may pair with the other

cases.name: 4090-transpose_operator_and_char
cases.trap:
Julia transposes a matrix by writing an apostrophe after it, so a' is an operation and the
apostrophe stands alone. A real character literal sits on the line below, and a counter that pairs
the two swallows everything between them

cases.name: 5010-line_splice_inside_a_string
cases.trap:
a backslash at the end of the line continues the string in C, so the // inside it is not a
comment

cases.name: 5020-blank_line_inside_a_spliced_string
cases.trap:
the splice carries a string only off a line ending in a backslash, and the blank line does not,
so the string is over before the comment line

cases.name: 5030-line_splice_inside_a_comment
cases.trap: a backslash at the end of a line comment continues it onto the next line in C

cases.name: 5040-line_splice_in_a_comment_with_no_words
cases.trap:
the splice of case 5030 on a comment line holding no letter or digit at all, which is how a
decorative rule is written. What a line says has no bearing on whether it continues

cases.name: 5050-line_splice_after_a_closed_block_comment
cases.trap:
a block comment closes and a line comment opens on the same line, with a space between the two.
That space is not code, so the splice ending the line still carries the comment on

cases.name: 5060-code_then_a_spliced_line_comment
cases.trap: a line holding real code ends in a spliced line comment, so the next line belongs to that comment in C

cases.name: 5070-blank_line_inside_a_spliced_comment
cases.trap:
a backslash at the end of a line comment carries it onto the blank line under it, so a line
holding nothing at all is still inside the comment. Blank to a counter that asks what the line
itself says, comment to one that asks what it is inside, and a counter that never sees the
splice does not face the question

cases.name: 6010-html_has_no_strings
cases.trap:
HTML has no strings of its own, so the apostrophe in the word it's is text like everything around
it and opens nothing

cases.name: 6020-comment_opener_inside_an_attribute
cases.trap:
a comment opener written inside a quoted attribute value, where HTML reads it as text. Nothing
closes it further down, so a counter that opened a comment there never ends one

cases.name: 6030-opening_tag_split_over_two_lines
cases.trap:
a script tag whose opening is split over two lines, which is legal HTML. A counter looking for the
whole tag on one line never sees it, and reads the JavaScript under it as markup

cases.name: 6040-script_tag_in_upper_case
cases.trap:
HTML reads its tag names without regard to case, so an upper case SCRIPT opens a script element
exactly as a lower case one does

cases.name: 6050-script_closer_written_with_a_space
cases.trap:
a closing script tag written with a space before its bracket, which is legal HTML and rare. A
counter looking for the tag without the space never finds the end of the block. Every count comes
out the same whether it found it or not, which is what keeps this one hidden

cases.name: 6060-script_closer_inside_a_string
cases.trap:
a script element ends at the first closing tag whatever the JavaScript around it is doing, which
is why one writes the closer with a backslash inside a string. So the block here holds no whole line,
and everything under the closer is markup, including what looks like a comment

cases.name: 6070-script_opener_that_never_closes
cases.trap:
the text of a script tag written inside a paragraph, with no closing tag anywhere after it.
Nothing marks an opener as a tag rather than the same word written out, so a block that never
closes is text and the rest of the file belongs to the page

cases.name: 6080-block_named_by_a_mime_type
cases.trap:
a script tag can name its language with a mime type instead of a lang attribute, and a mime type
spells the language out: 'text/typescript', not 'text/ts'. The counts are the same whichever
language answers, so what this case is about is the label

cases.name: 6090-vue_blocks_count_as_their_own_languages
cases.trap:
one file, three languages: the script and style blocks are counted with their own symbols, so
the js comment and the css comment are comments although the Vue file holding them has neither
symbol

cases.name: 6100-block_language_named_by_the_tag
cases.trap:
the opening tag names the language of its block, so this file is Vue, TypeScript and SCSS and not
Vue, JavaScript and CSS. Every count comes out the same either way, so nothing but the names
themselves can tell a counter that read the tags from one that guessed

cases.name: 6110-php_block_holding_html_around_it
cases.trap:
the file switches language at a tag rather than at a file boundary, and switches back at another
tag, so the markup between the two belongs to a language the extension does not name

cases.name: 6120-script_inside_html_inside_php
cases.trap:
three languages deep, the everyday shape of a page: the php file holds html between its blocks,
and the html holds a script. Every line belongs to the innermost language, and a tag's own line
to the language that encloses the tag, so the script tags are html and the html sits between the

cases.name: 7010-regex_literal_holding_a_quote
cases.trap:
a double quote inside a JavaScript regular expression, where it is part of the pattern and opens
no string. A counter fooled by it is left inside a string that nothing closes, and every line
under it goes the same way

cases.name: 7020-regex_holding_a_comment_opener
cases.trap:
a block comment opener inside a JavaScript regular expression. Knowing that the slash begins a
pattern and not a division takes reading what came before it, which is more than any counter here
attempts. What each of them does with the opener after that is its own

cases.name: 8010-punctuation_only_line
cases.trap:
a line holding only a brace. A definition, not a mistake: neither code nor comment to a counter
that asks what a line says, code to one that asks whether the file would compile without it

cases.name: 8020-blank_line_inside_block_comment
cases.trap:
a blank line inside a block comment. A definition, not a mistake: blank to a counter that asks
what a line says, comment to one that asks which block it sits in

cases.name: 8030-blank_line_inside_a_multiline_string
cases.trap:
a blank line inside a string that runs over several lines. A definition and not a mistake: blank
to a counter that asks what the line itself says, code to one that asks what the line is inside

cases.name: 8040-doc_comment_with_no_text
cases.trap:
a documentation line holding nothing but the /// that marks it, which is how a blank line is put
between two paragraphs of documentation. It is a comment to a counter that asks what the line is
inside, and neither code nor comment to one that asks what the line says, since it says nothing

cases.name: 8050-doc_comment_with_no_text_ending_a_block
cases.trap:
the same empty /// line as case 8040, this time the last one, with code and no more documentation
under it. A counter that decides an empty marker by what surrounds it has nothing to look at here,
and the answer has to come out the same, since the line itself has not changed

answers.note:
the block comment is cut out together with the line break inside it, so the code before the
opener and the code after the closer become one line and the line that vanished is charged to
comments

CMake has no bracket comment here, only the hash, which is a comment wherever the line's first
mark is one. So the opener's line is a comment and its body and closing bracket count as code

the inner closer ends the comment although Haskell's pair nests, so what follows it on that line
is left standing and the line counts as code

an opener that comes after a closer on the same line is not acted on, whether the two symbols
touch or a space separates them, so the block it reopens is never a comment

the inner closer ends the comment although Odin's pair nests, so the lines under it up to and
including the outer closer are left as code

a line whose first word begins with REM is taken as a comment whatever letters follow, so the
command counts as one

a // at the head of a line opens a comment inside a backtick template as readily as outside one,
so that line of template text counts as a comment

a triple quoted string is read as documentation wherever it opens, the middle of a line of code
included, so the lines holding its text and its closing quotes are added to the comment count

a triple quoted string is documentation wherever it opens, so the three lines of this block are
comments although the program prints their text

a // at the head of a line opens a comment inside a triple apostrophe string too, so that line

a string that opened on an earlier line does not stop a // from being stripped, so the line of

a blank line under a line ending in the language's continuation symbol is read as continuing it

a line comment stops at the line break whatever the line ends with, so the line spliced onto it

answers.note: the line counts as a comment although there is code on it

the line counts as code, because it opens a block and does not end with that block's closer. Any
number of blocks closed on one line ends the same way once a line comment follows them
the line counts as code, for the reason case 1070 gives, and the shared byte adds nothing
the block is never closed, so the rest of the file counts as comment
a line that began inside a block is a comment, so the statement after the close is lost

the whole of the first line is given to the documentation, so the code in front of the doc marker
is counted as a comment and lands in the Markdown block instead of in Rust

CMake has no bracket comment here, so the # opens a line comment that ends with its own line and
